security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, credential theft, or malicious data-exfiltration intent was found. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, scientific terms, and printed setup text. Confirmed risks are operational: shell commands, external downloads, Docker use, third-party demo links, and a user-selected CSV export path.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the DiffDock repository to a commit and the Docker image to a digest. Require user confirmation before any clone, pull, or run command.
Warn users before sending protein or ligand data to external services. Prefer local execution for private research data.

remediation.issue: CSV export writes to a user-selected path
remediation.suggestion: Confirm export destinations, avoid overwriting existing files, and reject sensitive system paths when possible.
Separate commands that mutate the environment from read-only examples. Mark each executable step as requiring explicit approval.

content.value_statement: Protein-ligand docking workflows can be hard to configure and interpret. This skill guides DiffDock setup, docking, screening, confidence analysis, and parameter tuning.
actual_capabilities: Guides DiffDock installation checks for Python, CUDA, RDKit, ESM, and model files.
Creates and validates batch CSV inputs for protein-ligand docking jobs.
Provides workflows for single docking, sequence-based docking, batch docking, and virtual screening.
Explains confidence score ranges and helps rank predicted binding poses.
Shows parameter tuning options for sampling, inference steps, temperatures, and batch size.
Documents integration paths for GNINA, MM/GBSA, OpenMM, and experimental validation.
limitations: It predicts binding poses and confidence, not binding affinity values.
It requires a working DiffDock installation and suitable compute resources.
Large ligands, flexible proteins, and membrane proteins need careful validation.
Results should be reviewed with structural checks and experimental evidence.

use_cases.title: Dock One Lead Compound
use_cases.description: Run a single protein-ligand docking workflow and review the top predicted poses.

use_cases.title: Screen Candidate Libraries
use_cases.description: Prepare batch inputs, run virtual screening, and rank compounds by confidence for follow-up review.

use_cases.title: Model Sequence-Based Targets
use_cases.description: Use protein sequences with ESMFold support when a prepared PDB structure is not available.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my DiffDock environment is ready. Explain any missing dependencies and the safest next setup step.

prompt_templates.title: Dock One Ligand
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me dock one ligand to one protein with DiffDock. Use my PDB path, ligand input, and desired output directory.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Batch Screening
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DiffDock batch workflow for my protein and ligand list. Include CSV validation, inference settings, and result review.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Advanced Parameters
prompt_templates.prompt: Optimize a DiffDock workflow for flexible ligands and uncertain poses. Recommend sampling, ensemble docking, scoring, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: I have a protein PDB file and an aspirin SMILES string.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a single docking workflow, an output folder, default sampling, and confidence review of the top poses.

output_examples.input: I need to screen 500 ligands against one target.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests validating a batch CSV, pre-computing protein embeddings, using GPU batches, and exporting ranked confidence summaries.

output_examples.input: My top poses have low confidence.
output_examples.output: The skill explains likely causes, suggests more samples or ensemble docking, and recommends rescoring and visual inspection.

best_practices: Verify the environment before large docking jobs.
Start with a small test complex before batch screening.
Use confidence scores as triage signals, not final binding decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat confidence scores as binding affinity measurements.
Do not send private molecular data to online demos without approval.
Do not run clone, Docker, or inference commands without checking paths and permissions.

faq.question: Does this skill predict binding affinity?
faq.answer: No. It predicts binding poses and confidence scores. Use scoring or experimental methods for affinity estimates.

faq.question: Can it work without a protein structure?
faq.answer: Yes, DiffDock can use a protein sequence with ESMFold support, but this adds time and uncertainty.

faq.question: Is a GPU required?
faq.answer: A GPU is strongly recommended. CPU runs can be much slower, especially for batch screening.

faq.question: What ligand formats are supported?
faq.answer: The workflows cover SMILES strings and ligand structure files such as SDF or MOL2 when RDKit can read them.

faq.question: How should I interpret confidence scores?
faq.answer: Higher scores suggest more reliable poses. They do not prove strong binding or biological activity.

faq.question: Can I use this for virtual screening?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes batch CSV preparation, embedding reuse, result ranking, and export guidance for screening campaigns.
